campaign.summary: Build hashing and stateful-API fundamentals first, then BFS/DFS before the concurrent web crawler, then linked lists and stacks before LRU caching and the sampling profiler. Practical multi-level builds are spread across the weeks and treated as full sessions, with the highest-weight Anthropic problems repeated as reviews. The final days before Dec 25 are consolidation only: timed redos of the signature problems and no new topics.

weeks.goal: Fluently group, dedupe and serialize data with hash maps, ending with Find Duplicate File in System solved cleanly.
Build the in-memory database through all OA levels (including TTL and history) and design file dedup with size-then-hash streaming.
Master graph traversal with visited sets, then implement Web Crawler Multithreaded with thread-safe state and clean termination.
Implement an O(1) LRU Cache from scratch and convert stack samples into correct trace events, including recursion and same-timestamp edge cases.

advice: Treat the CodeSignal OA as a speed test. Code fast against the exact public API, get each level's tests passing, and expect later levels to force a refactor. Polish at the end.
Edge cases still matter. A candidate scoring about 770/800 was rejected, so check TTL boundaries, missing keys, and same-timestamp ordering.

Drill the small known question bank: in-memory DB, banking system, cloud file storage, web crawler (then concurrent), stack samples to trace events, file dedup, and the LRU/memoize cache made crash-durable.
Know your language's standard library cold. In Python that means threading, concurrent.futures, asyncio, hashlib, os/pathlib and collections. Practise thread-safe visited sets and clean termination.
After a working first version, expect follow-ups on concurrency, data larger than memory, real-time or streaming input, and persistence (WAL or disk). Rehearse how you'd discuss each.
Prepare seriously for the culture/values round: a specific 'why Anthropic' with a real example, plus your views on AI safety. Reports call it the hardest round.
company.interview_format: Typical 2025–2026 pipeline: a 90-min CodeSignal OA (one progressive 4-level project; a 6-part variant was reported in June 2026), a 30-min recruiter call, then a 45–60 min live coding screen on CodeSignal, Replit or Colab. That screen is one problem with escalating follow-ups. The virtual onsite has 4–5 rounds of about 1 hour each: 1–2 coding, 1–2 system design, hiring manager, and culture/values. Some 2026 loops add a PR-review round where Claude is available. The focus is practical engineering rather than classic DS&A: stateful APIs that evolve, hashing and file I/O, BFS plus concurrency, caching and durability, and scale follow-ups.

topic_weights.why: Almost every reported question is a practical build. Examples are the in-memory DB, banking system, file storage, profiler trace events, dedup with streaming, durable LRU, and PR review. Several sources say 'no leetcode' in the OA.
Hash maps and sets underpin the KV-store OA, file dedup (group by size, then content hash), and the crawler's visited set.
The web crawler is BFS over same-host URLs and is the top dataset problem. It was also reported in Sep 2025 screens and onsites.
Both the stack-samples to trace-events profiler question and Exclusive Time of Functions (dataset) need call-stack reasoning and prefix comparison.
The LRU cache (hash map plus doubly linked list) is the base of a reported onsite question that is extended to memoization and crash durability.
The in-memory DB has prefix-scan levels and a hashtag autocomplete title was reported. Evidence for a trie specifically is thin, so the weight is moderate.
Historical, timestamped lookups in the DB OA can use bisect. Otherwise reports say binary search is not asked.
The tokenizer question uses greedy longest-match, but it is a low-confidence report from aggregators only.
Only the low-confidence 'fair coin from biased coin' phone-screen title points here.
No reports. A candidate said to forget heaps for the OA.
No DP reported in any source.
